title: US backs power upgrades along the Lobito Corridor in DRC and Zambia
body: The US Trade and Development Agency has signed an agreement with Anzana Electric Group to fund a feasibility study for hydropower rehabilitation, new generation and expanded electricity distribution along the Lobito Corridor in the DRC and Zambia. The project targets Lualaba Province in the DRC and Zambia's North Western Province, aiming to improve power reliability for copper and cobalt mining while extending access to more than three million people. It is part of wider US support for the corridor, which moves critical minerals from Central Africa through Angola's Port of Lobito.

title: Ogun State and DP World sign $7bn Gateway Deep Sea Port and Blue Economy zone deal
body: Ogun State and DP World MEA FZE have signed MoUs for the Gateway Deep Sea Port and the Ogun State Blue Marine Special Economic Zone, with initial investment expected to exceed $7 billion and over 50,000 direct jobs projected. The port at Ogun Waterside will feature a four-kilometre berth with 18-metre draft, integrated with a 10,000-hectare special economic zone and linked by the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. President Tinubu said the projects aim to decongest the Lagos port corridor and expand Nigeria's manufacturing and export capacity.

title: Nigeria's $300m Distributed Renewable Energy Fund reaches commercial launch
body: The Nigeria Distributed Renewable Energy Fund, promoted by the NSIA, Africa50 and Sustainable Energy for All, moved from structuring to commercial deployment on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The World Bank is a founding partner with an initial $25 million IDA contribution, and the fund is co-managed by Africa50 and NSIA to finance mini-grids and solar home systems for underserved communities. Promoters frame it as a country-level demonstration linked to Mission 300's goal of connecting 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030.

title: WIOCC Group secures $300m from AFC and Vision Invest to expand Africa digital backbone
body: Carrier-neutral digital infrastructure platform WIOCC Group has secured a combined $300 million via a shareholder subscription agreement with Africa Finance Corporation and Vision Invest, signed at the LEAP 2026 exhibition in Riyadh. The investment will accelerate data-centre deployment and consolidation, expand open-access terrestrial fibre across the continent, and fund new subsea assets. WIOCC operates in more than 30 African countries.

title: Rwanda and Pakistan sign trade cooperation pact at Kigali investment forum
body: Rwanda and Pakistan signed a Trade Cooperation Agreement at the Rwanda-Pakistan Investment Forum 2026 in Kigali to expand bilateral trade and investment and promote local production, with cooperation on trade facilitation, manufacturing and technology. Bilateral trade reached US$236.4 million between 2023 and 2025, and Rwanda hosted seven Pakistani investment projects worth over US$2 million in that period. Rwanda is seeking greater Pakistani investment in agro-processing, textiles and pharmaceuticals.

title: World Bank: behind-the-border barriers, not tariffs, are the biggest brake on African trade
body: A new World Bank report, Integrating Africa from Threads to Hubs, finds about 60% of Africa's trade costs come from unilateral behind-the-border barriers such as customs inefficiencies, unaligned standards and poor infrastructure, rather than tariffs. Only 15-17% of Africa's exports stay within the continent, and intra-regional trade intensity has declined since 2018. The report urges AfCFTA to move from legal commitments to functional integration, saying deeper trade agreements could raise exports by up to 56%.

title: Dangote breaks ground on $660m Ethiopia-Djibouti refined-fuel pipeline at Damerjog
body: Ethiopia and Djibouti joined the Dangote Group at a groundbreaking for the $660 million Damarjog-Dewele Oil Terminal and Pipeline Project in the Damerjog Free Trade Zone. The 120-kilometre multiproduct pipeline will link marine storage at Damarjog with inland storage at Dewele on the Ethiopian border, with plans for roughly 375,000 cubic metres of storage in Djibouti and 800,000 cubic metres in Ethiopia, targeting operations within about 18 months. The presidents of both countries framed it as a boost to regional integration and Horn of Africa energy security.

title: Malawi rules out devaluation as it courts a new IMF programme
body: Malawi Finance Minister Mwanamvekha has ruled out devaluing the kwacha while an IMF mission is in the country negotiating a possible new funding arrangement. The World Bank's latest Malawi Economic Monitor credited the government with executing the 2026/27 budget within approved limits for the first time in over five years, cutting the primary deficit from 3.7% to 0.4% of GDP, but projects only 2.7% growth this year with inflation and foreign-exchange distortions still weighing on investment and jobs.

title: Ogun State and DP World sign $7bn deep sea port and special economic zone deal
body: Ogun State and DP World MEA FZE signed MoUs for the Gateway Deep Sea Port and the Ogun State Blue Marine Special Economic Zone, with initial investment of over $7 billion and more than 50,000 direct jobs projected. The port at Ogun Waterside will have a four-kilometre berth and 18-metre draft to decongest the Lagos port corridor, and is linked by a 28-kilometre section of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. The 10,000-hectare zone is designed to support manufacturing, processing and export-oriented industries.

title: Guinea launches ~$455 million domestic bond for Simandou 2040 program
body: Guinea's government is launching a public bond offering of 2,500 billion Guinean francs (about US$455 million) on 25 September in Conakry to fund the Simandou 2040 program, arranged by Afriland First Bank Guinea. The five-year issue carries an annual coupon and is part of the financing push around the giant Simandou iron ore development.

title: Tinubu at UNGA: Africa demands two permanent UN Security Council seats and financial-system reform
body: Addressing the UN General Debate on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima demanded at least two permanent Security Council seats for Africa — with veto rights — plus five non-permanent seats, invoking the Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration. He said the world of 2026 cannot remain captive to the 1945 distribution of power while Africa fills the Council's agenda from the margins, and called for a radical shake-up of the global financial system.

title: Nigeria and US sign framework to unlock investment in $700bn minerals sector
body: Nigeria and the United States signed a framework agreement, announced on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, to deepen American investment in Nigeria's solid minerals sector, estimated at about $700 billion. Cooperation covers geological data and exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure and technical capacity, with Nigeria pushing for local refining rather than ore exports. Solid Minerals Minister Dele Alake said the two countries will identify viable projects and mobilise investment in the months ahead.

title: Dangote breaks ground on $660m Ethiopia-Djibouti fuel pipeline
body: Dangote Group, Ethiopia and Djibouti launched the $660m Damerjog-Dewele Oil Terminal and Pipeline Project: a 120-kilometre multiproduct pipeline linking Djibouti's Damerjog port to storage and distribution at Dewele in Ethiopia, with about 400 million litres of storage, expected to begin operations within 18 months. Ethiopia's PM Abiy Ahmed said it will cut fuel transport from Djibouti to Addis Ababa from five days to one. The project is part of Dangote's Vision 2030 plan to invest $50 billion across Africa in industrial and energy infrastructure.

title: IMF projects 4.3% growth for sub-Saharan Africa in 2026, urges faster reforms and regional integration
body: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva urged African countries to accelerate reforms, pursue sound macroeconomic policies and deepen regional integration, presenting the continent as a unified investment destination. The Fund expects sub-Saharan Africa's economy to grow 4.3% in 2026, down from an estimated 4.5% in 2025, citing higher fuel, fertiliser and food prices, tighter global financing and geopolitical tensions. She also flagged Africa's young population and critical-mineral endowment as strategic advantages in the AI era.

title: Dangote taps India's Engineers India for $16bn, 700,000 bpd refinery in Lamu, Kenya
body: Aliko Dangote has signed a $450 million deal with Indian state-owned Engineers India Ltd to oversee construction of a planned $16 billion refinery and petrochemical complex in Lamu, Kenya, with 700,000 barrels-per-day capacity, per a Bloomberg-reported filing. Construction is targeted to begin by the end of September, extending Dangote's refining footprint from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean, alongside plans for pipelines linking Lamu and Djibouti to Ethiopia.

title: AfCFTA's Mene: Africa loses ~$5bn a year to third-currency conversion; PAPSS is the fix
body: AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene told the PMI Global Summit Series in Cape Town that Africa must strengthen its delivery capacity — payment systems, efficient borders and infrastructure — for businesses to benefit from continental trade. He estimated currency-conversion costs of roughly $5 billion annually because African businesses trading with each other often need US dollars, and pointed to the PAPSS local-currency payment system as the practical remedy.

title: UN launches critical-minerals Country Support Mechanism; Nigeria, Zambia, Zimbabwe among first beneficiaries
body: UN Secretary-General António Guterres announced a Country Support Mechanism on Critical Energy Transition Minerals, led by UNDP, to help resource-rich developing countries build sustainable mineral value chains. Nigeria, Guinea, Madagascar, Zambia and Zimbabwe are among the first countries to receive dedicated support for turning copper, lithium, cobalt and rare-earth wealth into jobs and value addition.

title: Nigeria's Oyedele: Africa needs cheaper, longer-term capital to close its infrastructure gap
body: Nigeria's Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said high financing costs, currency risks and what he called a 'stereotype tax' on African borrowers are constraining the continent's ability to fund energy and other critical infrastructure. He called for reform of global climate finance, simpler access to affordable capital, and greater international investment in gas and transition energy sources given Africa's large energy-access deficit.

title: Ecobank opens Dangote Refinery share offer to investors across 33 African countries
body: Ecobank is using its pan-African retail and digital banking network to let investors across 33 African countries, plus offices in London, Paris, Beijing and Dubai, subscribe to the ongoing Dangote Petroleum Refinery share offer, which opened 14 September and closes 13 October 2026. Shares are priced at 525 naira with a 10-share minimum, widening retail participation in one of the continent's largest industrial equity raises beyond Nigeria.

title: Ghana's Cocobod turns to domestic market for $1.4bn cocoa financing as syndicated-loan era ends
body: Ghana Cocoa Board is seeking to raise 16.3 billion cedis (about $1.4 billion) from domestic investors to fund cocoa purchases for the new season, per a government presentation to investors. A new special-purpose vehicle, Cocoa Capital PLC, is issuing an initial 2.3 billion cedi bond plus 4 billion cedis of commercial paper, with repayments backed by assigned cocoa export receivables. The shift ends reliance on the decades-old international syndicated-loan model that collapsed in the 2023/24 season, though licensed buyers say Cocobod still owes them about 4 billion cedis for last season's crop.

title: Zambia inflation eases to 6.1%, lowest since 2018, keeping door open for a fourth rate cut
body: Zambia's annual inflation fell to 6.1% in September from 6.2% in August — the lowest since February 2018 — helped by a stronger kwacha and temporary tax measures, Statistician-General Sheila Mudenda said in Lusaka. Food inflation slowed to 5.8% while monthly CPI rose 0.4%. The print sets the stage for a possible fourth consecutive Bank of Zambia rate cut, though the fuel-tax suspension and zero-rated VAT expire on September 30.

title: Kenya puts $600m price tag on institutional clean cooking as UNGA event kicks off Nairobi summit push
body: Kenya and Norway co-hosted the first high-level clean cooking event held on Africa's behalf during UN General Assembly week in New York, framing household energy as infrastructure rather than welfare. Kenya unveiled a $600 million institutional clean-cooking investment opportunity covering schools, health facilities and correctional institutions, and announced it will co-host the Second Africa Clean Cooking Summit in Nairobi on 27-28 January with Norway, the US and the IEA. The IEA estimates universal clean cooking access in Africa requires roughly $2 billion a year through 2040.

title: GSMA and PDAA launch roadmap to close Africa's 906-million-person mobile internet usage gap by 2030
body: The GSMA and the Partnership for Digital Access in Africa launched a UNGA-week roadmap targeting one billion meaningfully connected Africans by 2030, prioritising migration from 2G/3G to 4G/5G smartphones, integrating energy and connectivity investment, and cutting the cost of rural coverage. About 906 million Africans — nearly 60% of the continent — live within mobile broadband coverage but do not use the internet, versus 122 million with no coverage at all. Halving the usage gap across the 11 studied markets would bring roughly 245 million more people online.

title: Nigeria and US sign framework to draw American investment into Nigeria's $700bn mineral sector
body: Nigeria and the United States signed a framework agreement at UNGA to attract American investment into Nigeria's estimated $700 billion mineral sector, covering exploration, processing, infrastructure and technical capacity building. Solid Minerals Minister Dele Alake and US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau signed in New York, with the next phase focused on identifying viable projects and mobilising commercial partnerships. Nigeria says the goal is local processing and value addition rather than raw-mineral exports.

title: Ethiopia, Djibouti and Dangote plan $660m refined-petroleum pipeline between the two countries
body: Ethiopia, Djibouti and the Dangote Group plan a $660 million, 120-kilometre refined petroleum pipeline to cut fuel transport costs along the Ethiopia-Djibouti corridor, with about 375,000 cubic metres of storage at Damerjog in Djibouti and 800,000 cubic metres at Dewele in Ethiopia. Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said the project, developed by Ethiopian Investment Holdings and Dangote, is expected to become operational within 18 months. Dangote is separately building a $4 billion fertiliser plant and power facility in Ethiopia.

title: Nigeria's Ima gas field gets $800m FID after 53 years, to feed NLNG Train 7
body: AMNI International and TotalEnergies took an $800 million final investment decision on the long-shelved Ima gas field in OMLs 112/117 off Rivers State, with first gas targeted for end-2028. The project is expected to deliver up to 350 MMscfd at plateau and supply about one-third of the feedgas for Nigeria LNG's Train 7, with roughly 77% of financing from Nigerian banks.

title: South Africa weighs $8bn revival of SAPREF and Mossel Bay refineries
body: The Central Energy Fund is advancing a plan that could see more than $8 billion invested to revive the mothballed SAPREF refinery in Durban (estimated at ~$7.15bn, potentially expanded from 180,000 to 400,000-650,000 bpd) and restart PetroSA's Mossel Bay gas-to-liquids plant in phases, with an FID targeted for 2027/28. Imported fuels now supply over 60% of South Africa's market.

title: Lesotho becomes first country to implement the UN AI blueprint, starting its 2026-2029 National Compute Roadmap
body: Prime Minister Samuel Ntsokoane Matekane told the second UN Digital Cooperation Day in New York that Lesotho has moved from planning into Phase One of its National Compute Roadmap, the first country anywhere to implement the UN master plan for AI. He argued the digital divide is now about computing power, data and skills rather than just internet access, and said Lesotho will build systems suited to its own resources, with infrastructure following demand.

title: South African Reserve Bank raises repo rate a quarter point to 7.25% as fuel-price shock intensifies
body: The South African Reserve Bank lifted its repo rate by 25 basis points to 7.25%, taking prime lending to 10.75%, with Governor Lesetja Kganyago saying the fuel-price shock has intensified. The surprise hike adds to borrowing costs for households and firms just as the continent's largest industrial economy tries to revive growth.

title: TotalEnergies takes FID on Ima gas field to feed Nigeria LNG Train 7 expansion
body: TotalEnergies and partner AMNI have taken the final investment decision on the Ima gas field in shallow water near Bonny Island, to be developed with a single platform tied by a 22 km pipeline to Nigeria LNG. Production is expected to start in 2028 at a plateau of 350 million cubic feet per day, supplying about one third of the gas for the Train 7 expansion that lifts Nigeria LNG capacity from 22 to 30 million tonnes per year.

title: Nigeria reopens talks on 3,050 MW Mambilla hydropower project after arbitration win
body: The Federal Government has opened fresh discussions with Energy China on a phased delivery of the 3,050 MW Mambilla Hydropower Project, after Nigeria successfully defended a 2.3 billion dollar arbitration claim by Sunrise Power that had stalled the project for years. Power Minister Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe said the government asked Energy China to examine the most practical delivery model, and that a recent power mission to China secured commitments from Sinomach, CMEC and CNEEC for priority projects including the 1.9 GW Presidential Power Initiative and the Zungeru evacuation scheme.

title: Africa takes 44.5% of JPMorgan new $328bn frontier bond index
body: JPMorgan is set to launch its Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets Edge (GBI-EM Edge) by the end of September, tracking about $328 billion of local-currency government debt across 26 markets - and Africa will account for 44.5% of the benchmark, the largest regional component, ahead of Asia at 31.5%. Egypt and Morocco each carry the maximum 8% country weighting, with Nigeria at 7.4%, Kenya at 6.91% and Tunisia at 5.32%. Inclusion signals African local-currency debt markets have grown large and accessible enough for global frontier benchmarks, potentially lifting foreign investor flows.

title: AfDB approves up to $5.1bn framework to counter energy and fertilizer shocks
body: The African Development Bank Board approved the Global Energy and Fertilizer Crisis Response Framework, unlocking up to $5.1 billion - $4.1 billion in additional AfDB lending and up to $960 million from the concessional African Development Fund - to help countries absorb global energy and fertilizer price shocks. The framework lifts the Bank Group 2026 lending target to roughly $12.7 billion and is designed to deliver rapid, targeted support while strengthening resilience against future shocks.

title: PAPSS to link with Egypt InstaPay as six Egyptian banks apply for integration
body: Afreximbank-backed PAPSS plans to connect its pan-African payment and settlement system to Egypt InstaPay, with six Egyptian banks already applying to the Central Bank of Egypt for final integration approval. The link would let Egyptian traders settle with African counterparts in local currencies instead of routing through USD correspondent banks, cutting cost and settlement time. Egypt took a 4.35% share of intra-African trade in 2025, about $9.59 billion, per Afreximbank African Trade Report 2026.

title: CBN cuts policy rate by record 350bps to 23% in 'monetary reset'
body: Nigeria's central bank cut its monetary policy rate from 26.5% to 23% — a record 350-basis-point reduction — while retaining the cash reserve ratio at 45% for deposit money banks. Governor Olayemi Cardoso framed the move as a 'monetary reset' to improve policy transmission as the bank transitions to inflation targeting. Analysts called it a calculated use of policy buffers.

title: Airtel Money confirms London listing after scaled-down targets
body: Airtel Money has confirmed its plan to float in London, targeted for October trading. The confirmation follows reports the mobile-money business is seeking to raise at least $800m at an $8-9bn valuation — well below the $1.5-2bn raise and $10bn valuation previously targeted. Airtel Africa shares fell 8.5% on the earlier report.

title: Dangote signs $450m deal with Engineers India to build Kenya's $16bn Lamu refinery
body: Engineers India Ltd., majority-owned by the Indian government, signed a $450m contract with Dangote to oversee construction of the planned 700,000 bpd greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Lamu, Kenya, with construction set to start this month. Engineers India said the project will strengthen East African fuel production and reduce import reliance. The plant complements the Lagos refinery, planned to double capacity to 1.4m bpd by 2029.

title: KG Mobility to build vehicle assembly plant in Ethiopia for East African export hub
body: South Korea's KG Mobility signed an MoU with Ethiopia's B&C Manufacturing Group and logistics firm Youngsan Glonet to build a knock-down assembly plant in Ethiopia. Construction starts in October with production in the first half of 2027, targeting about 1,000 units a year of models including the Torres EVX and Musso EV, with exports planned to Somalia, Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda and Djibouti.

title: ITC and Access Bank partner to boost SME finance across 14 African countries
body: The International Trade Centre and Access Bank's Access Africa office signed an MoU on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly to expand SME access to finance, skills training and markets in 14 African countries, with a focus on women- and youth-owned businesses. Implementation begins with a Ghana pilot from September 2026 to June 2027, scaling from 2027, including support for intra-African trade under AfCFTA.

title: South Africa needs $8bn+ to revive mothballed state-owned refineries
body: Officials told South African lawmakers that reviving two mothballed state-owned refineries will cost more than $8 billion, as the country seeks to strengthen energy security and cut dependence on imported fuels. The state Central Energy Fund, which bought the flood-damaged 180,000 bpd Sapref refinery from BP and Shell in 2024 for 1 rand, plans to upgrade it to a 400,000-650,000 bpd plant, with a Treasury-approved final investment decision targeted for 2027/28. Afreximbank financing is among options under discussion, though CEF provided no funding details.

title: Elumelu urges shift from aid to trade for Africa at UNGA
body: Speaking at the 81st UN General Assembly in New York, Heirs Holdings chairman Tony Elumelu called for a pivot in US-Africa relations from aid dependency to private-sector-led commercial partnerships, urging venture funds, pension managers and development finance institutions to partner with local African financial institutions to finance energy corridors and trade hubs. He argued that over 600 million Africans without electricity makes gas a necessary transition fuel, and that frameworks like AGOA should be modernised to cut production and freight costs as AfCFTA implementation deepens supply-chain integration.

title: Nigeria's finance minister flags 'prejudice premium' on African capital at UN climate finance dialogue
body: Finance minister Taiwo Oyedele told the UN Dialogue on Solutions to Climate Finance at UNGA that Africa's low contribution to global emissions has not spared it higher financing costs, describing a 'prejudice premium' and 'stereotype tax' on African borrowing. He called for simpler, more affordable financing arrangements for infrastructure and energy — including gas investment as transition energy — saying such investment would also diversify global energy supplies amid Gulf disruptions.

title: Uganda's Fine Spinners bets $5m on Kenya's AGOA apparel export market
body: Ugandan textile maker Fine Spinners Uganda is investing $5 million in new machinery to lift mill capacity by 30-40% — up to 40 tonnes of yarn and 200,000 garments a month — targeting Kenya's EPZ apparel exporters who currently import fabric from China and India. Kenya is central to the strategy because Uganda lost direct AGOA market access, so the firm uses Kenya's export infrastructure and third-country provisions to reach US buyers.

title: JPMorgan puts Africa at 44.5% of new $328bn frontier bond index
body: JPMorgan will launch its Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets Edge by the end of September, tracking about $328bn of local-currency government debt across 26 markets. Africa takes 44.5% of the benchmark - the largest regional allocation, ahead of Asia at 31.5% - spread across 10 countries, with Egypt and Morocco capped at 8% each, Nigeria at 7.4% and Kenya at 6.91%. Inclusion could steer passive flows toward African local debt markets and deepen their investor base.

title: Dangote hires Engineers India for $450mn of work on planned $15bn Lamu refinery in Kenya
body: Dangote Group has hired India's state-owned Engineers India as project management and EPCM consultant on a proposed 700,000 bpd refinery and petrochemical complex at Lamu, Kenya, part of the LAPSSET corridor. Kenya is preparing a September 30 groundbreaking, but no financial close has been announced and permitting, crude-supply and export infrastructure remain unresolved. The project is estimated at $15-16bn with completion targeted around 2030.

title: Côte d'Ivoire approves 8-year Zipline deal to reach 12 million people with drone health logistics
body: Côte d'Ivoire's government approved an 8-year public-private partnership with Zipline to expand its AI-powered medical drone delivery network from one hub in Daloa to ten nationwide, backed partly by a $150m US State Department pay-for-performance award. At full deployment the network should serve 2,200+ health facilities and over 12 million people - one of Africa's largest national AI/robotics healthcare deployments.

title: Afreximbank and GIIF sign project-preparation pact for Ghana's $11.5bn 24-Hour Economy pipeline
body: Afreximbank, the Ghana Infrastructure Investment Fund and Ghana's 24-Hour Economy Authority signed a Joint Project Preparation Framework Agreement to fast-track bankability of priority projects in the roughly $11.5bn 24H+ pipeline. Each institution contributes an initial $5m of project-preparation capital - for technical, legal and structuring work, not construction - spanning energy, logistics, industrial parks, agro-processing and minerals beneficiation.

title: Dangote hires Engineers India for $16bn, 700,000 bpd Lamu refinery in Kenya
body: Aliko Dangote has signed a $450m deal with India's state-backed Engineers India Ltd to oversee construction of a planned 700,000 barrel-per-day greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Lamu, Kenya, with construction set to start this month. The plant will complement Dangote's Lagos refinery, which is planned to double to 1.4 million bpd by 2029, and extends his footprint into East Africa while reducing the region's reliance on imported fuel.

title: Ex-Gold Fields CEO Chris Griffith lines up $1bn Africa critical-minerals fund
body: Former Gold Fields CEO Chris Griffith has joined a private equity venture raising $1 billion to invest in African critical minerals, four years after leaving the gold miner. The fund targets the copper, lithium, graphite and nickel projects the continent's energy-transition supply chains depend on.

title: Zimbabwe secures funding to upgrade Chirundu one-stop border post with Zambia
body: Zimbabwe's government announced a funding agreement with private-sector partners, the Chirundu Border Consortium, clearing the path for construction to upgrade the Chirundu crossing — Africa's first one-stop border post — on the North-South Corridor linking the Zambia-DRC Copperbelt to southern African ports. The gateway handles copper, cobalt, fuel and mining freight, and the upgrade aims to cut border delays.

title: South African Reserve Bank raises repo rate to 7.25% into fuel-price shock
body: The South African Reserve Bank raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 7.25% (prime 10.75%), effective 25 September, citing an intensified fuel-price shock and rising global rates, and cut its 2026 growth forecast to 1.2%. Governor Lesetja Kganyago called it a measured response in conditions of high uncertainty.

title: Tigray fighting escalates: Mekelle airport changes hands, Ethiopian Airlines suspends northern routes
body: Tigrayan forces took control of Alula Aba Nega International Airport at Mekelle overnight, and Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to Mekelle, Axum and Shire from 23 September, deepening the return to conflict in northern Ethiopia.

title: Nigeria launches $300m distributed renewable energy fund as World Bank commits $25m
body: The Nigeria DRE Fund, co-managed by NSIA and Africa50 with SEforALL, has reached commercial operation, moving from structuring to active capital deployment for mini-grids, solar home systems and storage. The World Bank joined as a founding partner with an initial $25 million IDA commitment. The fund is aligned with Mission 300, the World Bank-AfDB push to connect 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030, and is positioned as a country-level model replicable across Africa.

title: Dangote unveils $46-50bn Vision 2030 expansion; Lamu refinery groundbreaking set for Sept 30
body: At Unstoppable Africa 2026 on the UNGA sidelines, Aliko Dangote announced plans to invest $46-50 billion under the group Vision 2030 strategy, including doubling the Lagos refinery from 700,000 to 1.4 million barrels per day. Kenya President Ruto met Dangote and Africa Finance Corporation in New York to line up financing for the $15-16 billion East Africa Refinery in Lamu, with groundbreaking scheduled September 30 and construction around 30 months.

title: AU commissioner: Africa needs $64bn a year and cross-border power trade to close energy gap
body: African Union Infrastructure and Energy Commissioner Lerato Dorothy Mataboge told the Global Africa Business Initiative in New York that closing Africa electricity access gap, with roughly 600 million people unserved, requires about $64 billion annually. She pushed policy harmonisation and cross-border electricity trade under the African Single Electricity Market (AfSEM) plus a continental energy master plan to coordinate investment in transmission.

title: Afreximbank and ATDC sign $500m facility to move African commodities
body: The African Export-Import Bank and the Africa Trading and Distribution Company signed a $500 million Global Credit Facility to strengthen trade, logistics, warehousing and distribution of African commodities across the continent and international markets. It comes as intra-African trade rose 5.47% to $213.8bn in 2025.

title: IFC commits $200m to Volta Lake logistics corridor linking Ghana to the Sahel
body: The IFC agreed $200m in financing to extend a railway the final 7km to the Volta Lake shore, connect power and dredge the river, opening a logistics corridor to northern Ghana, Burkina Faso and other Sahelian states. AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene said recorded intra-African trade stood around $220bn in 2024.

title: Afreximbank issues $29m guarantee to scale the EAC digital Customs Bond
body: Afreximbank issued a $29m guarantee to BSMART Technology to scale the East African Community Customs Bond, a digital platform that lets clearing agents move goods across EAC borders without physical bond documentation at each border post. The Bond launched at the EAC Heads of State Summit in March 2026.

title: DFC joins AFC and Vision Invest in WIOCC digital infrastructure investment
body: The US International Development Finance Corporation joined the Africa Finance Corporation and Vision Invest in an investment in WIOCC Group to expand African digital infrastructure, including broadband connectivity and data-centre capacity across the continent.

title: Nigeria gives government 180 days to launch Digital Free Zones roadmap
body: President Tinubu directed the industry ministry to produce a roadmap within 180 days for the full launch of Nigeria Digital Free Zones, designed to let tech firms incorporate on Nigerian soil and raise international capital rather than defaulting to Delaware or UK entities. Itana, the first licensed digital free zone, anchors the plan alongside AFC backing.

title: Dangote commits $10bn to Africa's power sector over next three to four years
body: Aliko Dangote said Dangote Group will invest over $10 billion in Africa's power sector within the next three to four years, potentially shelving its steel project to redirect funds into electricity. He framed the move as a response to the 600 million Africans still without power, and also confirmed plans to list the group's businesses, including the Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO.

title: DR Congo plans one-stop agency to fast-track major mining investments
body: DR Congo is preparing a one-stop agency, led by its finance and economy ministries, to centralise registration, licensing, taxation and compliance for major mining projects, four sources told Reuters. The reform, tied to its minerals partnership with the US, would initially target joint ventures worth over $1 billion and aims to cut approval processes that can drag on for months.

title: Ruto: Africa's $2tn in domestic capital is blocked by rules, not scarcity
body: At a UNGA side event, Kenya's President William Ruto argued Africa holds over $2 trillion in domestic non-bank capital, including more than $1 trillion in pension and insurance assets, but restrictive prudential rules keep it out of productive projects. He cited a UNDP estimate that fairer credit ratings could save African countries up to $74.5 billion and called for reform of rules that treat long-term African investments as exotic assets.

title: Nigeria's CBN slashes policy rate by 350bps to 23% in historic 'reset'
body: The Central Bank of Nigeria cut its Monetary Policy Rate by a record 350 basis points, from 26.5% to 23%, at its 307th MPC meeting, recalibrating the standing facilities corridor to +50/-300bps while retaining the cash reserve ratio at 45% for deposit money banks. Governor Olayemi Cardoso framed the move as a 'reset and recalibration' to repair monetary transmission as August headline inflation eased to 15.39%, not a shift to broad easing. Markets expect cheaper credit and lower government borrowing costs.

title: Nigeria's economy grows 4.43% — its fastest in five years
body: Second-quarter growth was carried by services, telecommunications, finance and agriculture, while the trade surplus doubled to $9.5bn. Non-oil sectors now account for 96% of total output.
source: Semafor Africa · National Bureau of Statistics

title: Africa makes its case for a bigger role on the global stage
body: Leaders from business, government and global institutions convened in New York alongside the 81st UN General Assembly. The UN Secretary-General called for a permanent African seat on the Security Council and for the continent's critical minerals to generate local value and jobs rather than being exported raw.

title: $300m Nigeria Distributed Renewable Energy Fund reaches first close
body: Co-managed by the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority and Africa50, the fund will finance local clean-energy developers — solar mini-grids, home systems and storage — aligned to Mission 300's goal of connecting 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030.

title: Kenya: 90%+ renewable electricity, and a new critical-minerals facility
body: Kenya generates more than 90% of its electricity from renewable sources, and the US backed a critical minerals processing facility in a country holding untapped copper, graphite, lithium and nickel.

title: AfCFTA trade projected to reach $230bn this year
body: Intra-African trade under the Continental Free Trade Area keeps scaling, supported by continental payment rails that shift cross-border settlement away from correspondent banking.

title: Dangote Refinery IPO set to be Africa's largest share sale
body: Nigeria's SEC approved an offering expected to raise around $1.5–1.8bn, with plans to double the refinery's capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day — which would make it the largest single-train refinery in the world.

title: Africa's solar adoption projected to rise 45% this year
body: As energy independence becomes a strategic priority, several countries moved to expand both refining and generation capacity — with renewables adoption rising sharply across the continent.

title: AGOA extended through December 2028
body: Preferential duty-free access to the US market is preserved for eligible sub-Saharan exporters, giving textiles, apparel and agriculture a firmer footing for the next two years.

title: Fintech remains Africa's largest venture sector
body: African start-ups raised $1.35bn in the first half of 2026. Fintech took $556m (41%) and logistics $472m. Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Egypt have absorbed roughly 80% of all capital raised since 2019.
